A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SISOM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original active-learning experiments, OpenOOD evaluations, ablations, and feature-space analyses in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds pretrained-model comparisons, sensitivity experiments, OOD evaluation of active-learning checkpoints, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The five components remain: multilayer coverage, KL-gradient feature enhancement, distance ratios, energy-score fusion, and sigmoid-steepness optimization. Class-wise subset selection is also retained. The revised explanations and evaluations of existing components do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN active learning and the same OpenOOD dataset pairings. The added pretrained-model and AL-checkpoint experiments change initialization and evaluation procedures within retained data and tasks. Open-set active learning is discussed but explicitly remains unevaluated.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 1 and 5 add SCALE, CombOOD, NNGuide, FeatureNorm, and RankFeat to the corresponding OpenOOD comparisons. The new pretrained CIFAR-10 comparison also evaluates PT4AL, TypiClust, and ProbCover alongside retained methods. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Reported query sizes change from 5,000 to 2,000 for CIFAR-100 and from 1,000 to 500 for SVHN. Appendix B.1 changes CIFAR-10/SVHN training from learning rate 0.1 with multistep scheduling to 0.025 with cosine scheduling. New protocols include SIMCLR initialization, ResNet34, additional query budgets, AL-checkpoint OOD evaluation, runtime measurements, and aggregate benchmark rankings. These are reported setting changes, not proof that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds query-size sensitivity, medium-data and model-size analyses, a UMAP examination of unlabeled/OOD overlap, intermediate-cycle OOD evaluation, and runtime/subset-size tradeoffs. The earlier feature-enhancement plots and sigmoid/subset ablation remain in v3 Figure 11, Figure 12, and Table 3; their relocation is not additional evidence.

E5.justification: v3 introduces uncertainty bands in the full-cycle OOD plots and ± quantities in runtime tables, although their statistical meaning is not clearly specified. Appendix B.2 identifies three seeds for the new full-cycle experiment. Existing AL standard-error reporting and three-seed CIFAR OpenOOD averaging remain; no increase in repetitions for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the expanded comparisons and analyses. Reported CIFAR-100 SISOMe near/far AUROC changes from 80.96/79.80 to 81.10/80.16, while NAC changes from 72.00/86.56 to 75.90/86.98. SISOMe's unchanged ImageNet near-OOD score of 78.59 falls from first to third with added comparators. AL curves are revised under changed settings, and the earlier OOD tables' classification-accuracy entries are removed.

T1.justification: The formal AL/OOD setup, distance definitions, score equations, and sigmoid optimization remain substantively unchanged. Gradient notation is clarified, but no new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is introduced. Aggregate benchmark ranking is an evaluation change.

C1.justification: v3 drops the explicit contribution of being first to explore the AL/OOD connection and elevates the existing latent-space refinement and self-balancing fusion to named contributions. Its headline OOD claim narrows from two first places and one second place to one first place and two top-three placements specifically for near-OOD. The conclusion expands its AL performance claim to eight benchmark settings.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly explains why the shared metric cannot independently solve open-set AL: informative unlabeled samples and OOD samples can be ambiguous. It adds discussion of top-k batch-diversity limitations, pretrained feature-space benefits, computational disadvantages, and why smaller reference subsets might remove outliers. These materially expand applicability boundaries and mechanism interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 adds project-page/code access information, SIMCLR initialization details, runtime hardware, full-cycle checkpoint sourcing, and UMAP construction details. These incrementally extend the existing experimental documentation. Most sigmoid parameters and search settings are retained and reformatted into tables; the linked resources' availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially expands to open-set AL, DDU, pretrained AL approaches, and newer OOD methods. v1's broad assertion that existing methods had not been evaluated on both tasks is replaced by acknowledging such uncertainty approaches and distinguishing SISOM through shared metrics and the application life cycle. This materially revises its research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, motivation, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries move ahead of related work, experimental subsections are reorganized, and Appendix A becomes a larger collection of experiments with the original qualitative material retained as A.4. These changes exceed routine copyediting.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document layout, redraws the life-cycle diagram, adds several plots and runtime tables, and replaces main AL accuracy plots with differences relative to random selection. Separate OOD tables become consolidated comparisons, with far-OOD results moved to the appendix. Parameter lists become tables. Some presentation defects remain, including Figure 1's caption overlapping body text.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v1 by directly testing OOD detection after AL training, measuring runtime and subset tradeoffs, broadening comparisons, and examining sensitivity to budgets and models. Its explicit open-set AL boundary also clarifies what the unified method supports. Reporting inconsistencies temper these gains: Appendix A.5 claims first place for CIFAR-10 far-OOD despite Table 5 showing FeatureNorm at 95.59 versus SISOMe at 94.74. Nevertheless, the added validation and clearer applicability substantially improve the paper overall.
